about: Slice 6 (docs/moth-10): the moth's textures and wear, by the texture loop (docs/texture-loop) as the J-Class's slice 11 (docs/jclass-11). One card per surface the plan names (carbon, the wings' mesh, the clear film sail) and the rest of her (the hull's and foils' paint, the alloy fittings, the Dyneema lines and shrouds, the grip): which of her materials it covers (by kind), the closest a camera comes, the pattern's real size, the detail maps it draws (her own, made by textures.py, or the boats' shared library), and what each of the loop's five wear levels (Tools/texloop/levels.json) looks like on her. How much of each wear term a level gets is weathering_moth.py's (amounts), from the loop's time and dirt numbers (Tools/texloop/wear.py).
water: Lake Ray Hubbard: fresh water (no salt crust, the lake's third of the salt-water corrosion rate), and she lives ashore on her trolley between sails, so no weed or barnacles: the foils and the hull's bottom only take a scum line where she was left in

levels.L0: new from the builder: deep glossy clear coat over the twill, white hull paint, satin grey foils, black wing mesh, a crystal-clear film sail, bright braid, satin silver anodising, a black grip
levels.L1: her first season: hairline scratches in the clear coat where the boom, the wand and hands touch, trolley scuffs on the hull's bottom, a little dust in the mesh, the first crease lines in the film at the battens, the braid's cover a touch fuzzy
levels.L2: six years a club boat, half kept: the clear coat dull and hazed with fine scratches all over and amber on the sun side, scuffs and tape residue on the hull, white filler on the foils' leading-edge dings, the mesh faded charcoal and dusty, the film milky and crinkled, grey fuzzy lines, the anodising dull and scratched to bright metal on its edges, the grip worn shiny
levels.L3: an early foiler kept thirty years: refinished, polished and with a new sail and lines, but the clear coat gone amber and the white paint faded cream, the anodising faded, the old filler repairs showing through the foils' paint
levels.L4: twenty years in a yard: the clear coat chalked white and flaking so the weave shows grey and fuzzy, chalky hull paint with black streaks from the fittings, the foils' paint chipped to filler and primer, the mesh grey-brown and mildewed, the film yellow-brown with black mildew specks and white creases, grey-green lines, white powder on the alloy, the grip chalky and cracked

carbon.title: Carbon
carbon.what: 3K twill under a clear coat on every tube and spar (the wings' frame, the gantry, mast, boom, tiller and its extension, the wand, the bowsprit), and the sail's battens
carbon.closest_camera_note: the tiller extension in the sailor's hand and the wing bar under the helm camera

levels.L0: a deep glossy clear coat, the twill's tows lit or dark by which way they run
levels.L1: hairline scratches where hands, the boom and the wand touch; the gloss otherwise new
levels.L2: the coat dull and hazed, fine scratches all over and polished where hands go, an amber cast on the faces the sun sees
levels.L3: refinished glossy, but the coat gone amber with the years
levels.L4: the coat chalked white and flaking in patches, the weave grey and fuzzy where it is gone, grime in the scratches

refs.note: carbon fibre twill (CC0): the new weave's colour

paint.title: Hull and foil paint
paint.what: The hull's white paint (topsides, bottom and transom) and its deck's paint and non-skid patches; the foils' and struts' satin grey paint (main strut and foil, flap, rudder, elevator, the junction's pod, the wand's paddle)
paint.closest_camera_note: the bow and the wand's fitting from the dock; the main foil from a camera at the water

levels.L0: white hull paint with a wet gloss, crisp non-skid, satin grey foils
levels.L1: trolley scuffs along the bottom and the chines, a faint scum line where she sat in, the deck's grip dusty
levels.L2: the paint dull and chalky, grey scuffs at the bow and along the bottom, tape residue round the foil case, black marks from fittings; the foils' leading edges dinged and filled with white filler, scratches along the span
levels.L3: polished, but the white faded cream; the foils' old filler repairs showing through their paint
levels.L4: heavily chalked paint with black streaks running from every fitting and a green-brown scum line; the foils chipped to filler and grey primer, their paint chalky

mesh.title: Wing mesh
mesh.what: The wings' open mesh, PVC-coated polyester strands in a plain weave, laced to the frame
mesh.closest_camera_note: the wing under the sailor's knees in the helm camera

levels.L0: black and evenly sheened, light through every gap
levels.L1: a little dust caught in the weave near the hull
levels.L2: faded to charcoal grey, dusty, worn shiny where the knees go
levels.L3: mesh a few seasons old (a kept boat re-meshes every six or so): a little faded
levels.L4: grey-brown and stiff, dusty, black mildew in patches

sail.title: Clear film sail
sail.what: The main's laminate (clear film over a polyester scrim) and its luff sleeve
sail.closest_camera_note: the foot and clew from the helm camera

levels.L0: crystal clear, the scrim's threads a faint grid
levels.L1: the first fine crease lines near the battens
levels.L2: milky and crinkled, a faint yellow
levels.L3: a kept boat's sail is renewed every few seasons: clear, with a few soft creases
levels.L4: yellow-brown, milky with white creases, black mildew specks between the layers

rope.title: Dyneema lines and shrouds
rope.what: Her braided lines (mainsheet, vang, cunningham, the shock cord, the lacing) and the uncovered Dyneema shrouds and forestay
rope.closest_camera_note: the mainsheet in the sailor's hand

levels.L0: bright orange lines and pale grey shrouds, a tight shiny braid
levels.L1: the cover a touch fuzzy where it runs through blocks
levels.L2: faded and grey with grime, fuzzy
levels.L3: lines a season or two old on an old boat: a little faded
levels.L4: grey-green, stiff and fuzzy, mildew specks

alloy.title: Alloy fittings
alloy.what: The anodised alloy fittings: the wand's head, the bellcrank's housing, the rudder's head, the blocks, the rig's fittings
alloy.closest_camera_note: the wand's head and the mainsheet's ratchet

levels.L1: the first scratches on the edges
levels.L2: dull and faded, edges scratched to bright metal
levels.L4: dull grey with white aluminium oxide in the crevices and round the screws

grip.title: Twist grip
grip.what: The rubber twist grip on the tiller extension and its universal joint
grip.closest_camera_note: the helm camera looks at it in the hand

levels.L1: a faint shine where the hand holds it
levels.L2: worn shiny and grey with grime in the ribs
levels.L3: a grip a couple of seasons old, a faint shine
levels.L4: chalky grey, cracked, grime in the ribs

maps.about: Her own maps are made by textures.py into Inputs/moth-detail (plain git, as Inputs/jclass-detail); the shared ones are the boats' library (Inputs/boat-detail), already in the game's memory for the J/22, so they cost her nothing more. Every map is sampled at its real size (tile_mm): the carbon round each tube by its own Tube UV (along the tube and round it), the rest box-projected in each part's frame, and the fine detail fades out between fade_m metres from the camera.

CarbonTwill.note: 3K tows of 12.5 to the inch (2.03 mm), a 2x2 twill repeating every four

WingMesh.note: an open PVC-coated polyester mesh, 1.0 mm strands on a 2.5 mm pitch (a third open: round 1's reviewers read the 1.6 mm pitch as a solid tarp)

Scrim.note: an X-ply style scrim: diagonals both ways 25 mm apart, a thread along the length 12.5 mm apart

Gelcoat.use: the hull's and foils' paint: orange peel and buffing marks

Metal.use: the anodised fittings' brushing and pits

budget.about: Texture memory: her own maps only, the shared library being resident for the J/22 already. Block-compressed with mips: BC5 normals (1 byte a pixel) and BC1 masks (half a byte), times 4/3 for the mips, at full size on High and Ultra; Medium draws no detail maps on her (the colour and roughness math only, as the boats' Medium material). Cap: 4 MB on High and Ultra, 0 on Medium.

views.about: The wear views, each [camera, target, lens mm] in Blender's frame (x forward, y to port, z up, metres), rendered at every level lit, as albedo and once as material ids; a surface's ladder is its crop of the view that shows it best (ladder).
